items.item_text: resume

Supports UC ANR Innovate and the CA AgTech Alliance by engaging startups, entrepreneurs, and researchers developing technologies relevant to California's agriculture and food systems. Working closely with program leadership, the position assesses innovator needs, develops industry and research partnerships, and connects partners with relevant expertise, programs, facilities, funding opportunities, and commercialization resources. The candidate coordinates exploratory discussions, field trial partnerships, and company participation in field days and other innovation programming. The position also helps build a statewide field trial network and supports events and outreach that connect innovators with growers, researchers, and other potential end users.

Working closely with UCANR Innovate Leadership, plan and carry out outreach to startups, entrepreneurs, researchers, and other innovators developing technologies relevant to California agriculture and food systems through conferences, field days, meetings, referrals, targeted research, and direct contact.

The UC ANR Innovate Statewide Program advances transformative solutions at the intersection of climate, food, farming, energy, and the bioeconomy. Through industry partnerships, applied research commercialization, and workforce development, the program accelerates the translation of innovation into real-world impact. UC ANR Innovate supports scalable, place-based agrifood innovation ecosystems across California, strengthening economic resilience, sustainability, and global competitiveness.
Assess technology focus, development stage, potential users, validation needs, and alignment with UC ANR and Alliance priorities; recommend promising opportunities for partnership or referral.
This position is a career appointment that is 100% fixed and ends on January 31, 2028 with the possibility of extension if funding permits.
Build and maintain industry and research partnerships to connect companies, growers, and ecosystem partners with relevant programs, expertise, services, funding, and commercialization resources.

This position may be eligible for a hybrid work arrangement, combining remote work with on-site work at the designated office in Madera, CA. Candidates must be available to work on-site at least two days per week, with additional on-site work and travel as business needs require.
Represent UC ANR Innovate’s programs, in particular the CA AgTech Alliance at assigned industry meetings and events, explain available resources, and identify opportunities for collaboration.
Pay Scale: $85,575.00/year to $121,590.00/year
Coordinate requests from startups, entrepreneurs, and researchers; understand their needs and connect them with relevant expertise, programs, facilities, and service providers.
Job Posting Close Date: This job is open until filled. The first application review date will be 12/9/2026.
Serve as the company liaison for Connect and other innovation programming field days. Coordinating logistics between companies / innovation teams and research and extension centers.
Build relationships with advisors, specialists, research centers, and principal investigators to identify opportunities to work with innovators.

Introduce innovators to researchers and potential end users when technologies align with applied research, demonstrations, or field validation. Follow up to determine whether the connections lead to useful next steps.
Coordinate exploratory meetings and the partnership aspects of proposed field validation projects, including goals, roles, schedules, action items, and progress updates.

Build and maintain a statewide field trial network across the UC ANR REC system and other relevant test sites, developing clear pathways to match companies with appropriate locations, technical expertise, growers, and research partners.
Support the organization and hosting of partner meetings and small group discussions that bring together innovators, growers, food producers, researchers, and other potential end users.
Communicate program opportunities and partnership needs to UC ANR Innovate communications staff; provide accurate program information and partner stories for approved outreach materials.
Maintain accurate records, respond to routine partner inquiries, and coordinate follow-up with colleagues and external partners.
Perform other related duties as assigned to support evolving program needs.
